title: 3 Lead Generation Strategies Every Fitness Business Can Automate

facts.fact: The article was last updated on December 11, 2023 and is listed as a 5-minute read.
The article's illustrative example prices a gym's one-week trial coupon at $5, presented as a hypothetical ("Let's pretend").
facts.quote: Let's pretend you want to offer a $5 one-week trial to your gym.

facts.fact: The article gives an example of a low-risk introductory fitness offer as an introductory two-class session with a trainer.
facts.quote: maybe you offer an introductory two-class session with a trainer.

facts.fact: According to the article, Keap Ultimate customers can start from Keap's built-in "Surprise Gift" campaign and adjust it to deliver a coupon.
facts.quote: If you are a [Keap Ultimate](https://keap.com/keap-max-classic) customer, you can start with the "[Surprise Gift]

facts.fact: Keap's Help Center offers a pre-built "Customer Survey" campaign that the article says needs little modification for collecting referral-appropriate feedback.
facts.quote: you can start with the "[Customer Survey](https://help.keap.com/help/play-blueprint-31004-customer-survey)" campaign found in the Help Center.

facts.fact: The article's referral guidance says referral requests should only go to customers who are happy and satisfied, and neutral or unsatisfied customers should be handled differently.
facts.quote: You only want to solicit referrals from customers who are happy and satisfied with their services so far.

facts.fact: The article recommends a two-part scheduling flow in which a website form collects a name and email and the Thank You page then shows the trainer's calendar for booking a free consultation.
facts.quote: The first part is collecting someone's name/email using a form and then part two (the Thank You page) is the trainer's calendar.
